procs.rm: Bauxite ore (ROM, alumina-grade), waste rock
procs.out: Crushed bauxite (-25mm typical) to refinery feed
procs.q: Available alumina (Al2O3)%, reactive silica%, moisture%, Fe2O3%, TiO2%

loc: Crusher discharge to stockpile conveyors (real-time quality grading)
Blending bay where multiple ore lots converge
Refinery feed conveyor (final quality checkpoint before digestion)
d: Analyses overhead camera feeds, NIR/LIBS sensors and online XRF data at conveyor lines.
Detects high-reactive-silica zones (the key cost driver in Bayer) and high-iron lots; sorts by grade.
Provides blending advisory and triggers diverter action for off-spec lots before refinery feed.
p: Lab silica analysis has 4-8 hour lag, too slow for blending decisions
Inconsistent bauxite feed causes Bayer process upsets and yield drops
High reactive silica lots silently increase NaOH cost without visibility
Manual blending decisions depend on operator judgment
Customer complaints on alumina quality traced back to bauxite variability
uc.calc: NaOH savings 5-10 kg/t alumina × ₹35/kg × 1.92 t alumina/t Al × 1 MTPA = ₹3-6 cr. Plus extraction efficiency uplift. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses GPS/telematics on haul trucks, shovel loading times, dispatch system data, and pit conditions.
Detects fleet utilization gaps, sub-optimal hauling routes, and shovel/truck mismatch.
Provides real-time dispatch optimization and operator coaching for throughput improvement.
p: Trucks queuing at shovels (capacity waste)
Empty hauls and sub-optimal routes
Operator productivity varies between shifts
Maintenance breakdowns disrupt fleet plans
Dispatch decisions made without real-time visibility
uc.calc: Fleet productivity 3-5% improvement + diesel consumption reduction. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

loc: Primary and secondary crusher feeds (oversize rocks, blasting debris)
Stockpile-to-refinery trunk belts (single-point failure for refinery feed)
d: Analyses camera images of belt surfaces, vibration on idlers, overhead camera feeds and metal detector signals.
Detects belt tears, mis-tracking, bearing degradation, tramp metal and oversize rocks.
Provides location-tagged alerts before crusher damage or belt failure.
p: Long bauxite conveyors fail with limited warning
Crusher damage from foreign material causes major shutdowns (₹50 lakh-1 cr/event)
Belt damage often noticed only on inspection rounds
Manual belt inspection cannot cover 24/7 operation
Stockpile-to-refinery line failure halts refinery feed
uc.calc: Belt failure prevention + crusher damage prevention. ₹1 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Crushed bauxite, spent liquor (NaOH recycled) + makeup NaOH
procs.out: Sodium aluminate slurry (pregnant liquor + red mud)
procs.q: A/C ratio, extraction efficiency%, digestion temperature, residual NaOH

d: Analyses bauxite feed quality (reactive silica, available alumina), digestion temperature, pressure, liquor concentration and residence time.
Models digestion kinetics and predicts extraction efficiency (% Al2O3 recovered from bauxite) versus operating conditions.
Provides advisory on temperature, A/C ratio and liquor flow for maximum extraction at minimum NaOH consumption.
p: Extraction varies 2-3% week-to-week due to bauxite quality variability
Operators manually adjust temperature/charge without optimization tools
Bauxite cost overruns from lower-than-expected extraction
Lab data lag (4-8 hr) prevents real-time response
Multiple parallel digesters operate at different extraction levels
uc.calc: Extraction improvement 1-2% × 4.5 t bauxite/t Al × ₹2,000/t bauxite = ₹90-180/t Al = ₹9-18 cr/MTPA. Capture 60% = ₹5-10 cr. Plus reduced makeup NaOH. ₹10 cr per MTPA aluminium.

uc.t: Digester Heat Exchanger Scale & Cleaning Optimization
d: Analyses overall heat transfer coefficient (U) trends across digestion heat exchangers, liquor flow/temperature, and scale buildup patterns.
Predicts scale buildup rates and remaining time-to-clean for each heat exchanger train.
Provides cleaning schedule optimization to maximize steam economy and digester availability.
p: Heat exchangers scale fast; cleaning frequency is reactive
Steam economy degrades 15-25% before cleaning
Cleaning shutdowns force throughput reduction
No predictive model for scale buildup vs bauxite changes
Mechanical cleaning is labor and chemical intensive
uc.calc: Steam economy improvement 5-10% on ₹50-80 cr digestion steam value. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Sodium aluminate slurry from digestion, flocculant
procs.out: Clarified pregnant liquor, red mud (residue) to disposal
procs.q: Overflow solids%, A/C ratio, soda losses to red mud, flocculant consumption

uc.t: Red Mud Settling & Soda Recovery Optimization
d: Analyses settler underflow density, overflow clarity, flocculant dosing rate, washer train counter-current performance and soda losses to red mud.
Models settling and washing efficiency; predicts soda losses per tonne red mud.
Provides flocculant dosing and washer operation advisory to minimize NaOH losses to red mud disposal.
p: Each washer stage performance varies; not optimally tuned
Flocculant overdosing common (operator caution)
Soda recovery declines as bauxite quality changes
Red mud disposal volumes constrained by storage capacity
High NaOH makeup cost without clear attribution to operations
uc.calc: Soda recovery improvement 3-5 kg Na/t Al × ₹40/kg + reduced flocculant. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

uc.t: Red Mud Disposal Compliance & Dry Stacking Optimization
d: Analyses red mud thickener output solids, filter press performance, transport conditions and dry stack moisture profile.
Detects compliance risks (pH, runoff potential), thickener underperformance and stacking anomalies.
Provides operational advisory and audit-ready compliance documentation.
p: Environmental compliance (state PCB) is sensitive and audited
Red mud area is regulator and community concern
Stacking moisture/density optimization is manual
Risk of runoff during monsoon
Storage area constraint forces operational adjustments
kpi: Dust emission events from stack area
uc.calc: Compliance penalty avoidance + dry stacking operational efficiency. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Pregnant liquor (sodium aluminate), seed crystals (Al(OH)3)
procs.out: Aluminium hydroxide crystals (Al(OH)3), spent liquor (recycled to digestion)
procs.q: Yield (g Al2O3/L), particle size distribution, soda in product, agglomerate strength

d: Analyses precipitation tank temperatures, seed addition rate, A/C ratio, agglomeration tank conditions and product PSD.
Models yield (g Al2O3/L), particle size distribution and product quality versus operating conditions.
Provides setpoint advisory for maximum yield with smelter-grade PSD targets.
p: Precipitation tank conditions drift over 24-48 hr cycle
PSD off-spec impacts smelter alumina quality
Yield variability constrains refinery throughput
Seed management depends on operator expertise
Temperature control balance is delicate
uc.calc: Yield improvement 2-3 g/L × refinery throughput × alumina margin. ₹6 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Aluminium hydroxide (Al(OH)3) hydrate
procs.out: Smelter-grade alumina (Al2O3) for potline, water vapor, fluidization gas
procs.q: LOI (loss on ignition)%, BET surface area (m2/g), α-alumina%, particle size, attrition index

d: Analyses fuel firing rate, air/fuel ratio, calciner temperature profile, flue gas O2/CO and alumina LOI/BET surface area.
Models calcining kinetics and predicts smelter-grade alumina (SGA) quality versus fuel consumption.
Provides fuel/air setpoint advisory for target LOI and BET with minimum fuel consumption.
p: Smelter alumina quality varies (LOI, BET) batch to batch
Fuel consumption higher than design specification
Manual fuel/air adjustments based on operator experience
Limited real-time alumina quality feedback (lab samples)
Calciner upsets cause smelter alumina supply variability
uc.calc: Fuel savings 3-5% on ₹100 cr calcination fuel + alumina quality premium downstream. ₹5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses kiln/calciner shell IR scanner data, thermal camera feeds and refractory thickness models.
Detects hotspots indicating refractory thinning and damage zones.
Provides location-tagged alerts and campaign life prediction.
p: Refractory failure forces unplanned shutdowns (₹2-5 cr/event)
Manual shell temperature checks miss developing hotspots
Campaign end timing is guesswork
Difficult to plan major maintenance when life is uncertain
uc.calc: Campaign extension + unplanned shutdown avoidance. ₹1.5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Spent liquor (recycled from precipitation), lime (CaO)
procs.out: Recausticized liquor returned to digestion, calcium aluminate residue
procs.q: Free caustic, total caustic (TC), free alkali to total ratio

d: Analyses spent liquor composition, lime addition rate, recausticization tank conditions and recycled liquor strength.
Models causticization efficiency and lime utilization; predicts recycled liquor strength.
Provides lime dosing setpoints to maximize CE without lime overdosing.
p: Liquor loop chemistry drifts; manual control
Lime overdosing common (operator caution)
NaOH makeup higher than thermodynamic minimum
Quality variability impacts upstream digestion
uc.calc: Lime savings + reduced NaOH makeup. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Calcined petroleum coke, coal tar pitch, recycled anode butts
procs.out: Green anode blocks (un-baked) for baking furnace
procs.q: Apparent density (g/cc), real density, blaine fineness, pitch absorption, green strength

d: Analyses petroleum coke quality, pitch properties, anode butt fraction, mixing temperature, vibroformer cycle and green anode density.
Models anode recipe versus baked anode properties (apparent density, resistivity).
Provides recipe and process setpoint advisory for consistent baked anode quality.
p: Coke and pitch quality variability causes inconsistent anodes
Recipe adjustments are slow (multiple shifts to test)
Baked anode rejects high (anode effect contributors downstream)
Anode butt recycling fraction not optimally managed
Lab feedback loop on anode properties is slow
uc.calc: Anode quality improvement reduces pot specific energy + reduced anode consumption. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Green anode blocks
procs.out: Baked anodes (target apparent density, low resistivity) to rodding
procs.q: Baked density (g/cc), specific electrical resistivity (μΩ·m), thermal shock resistance, cracks

d: Analyses fuel firing per section, draft control, baking curve adherence, section temperature profile and finished anode quality.
Models baking kinetics across the ring furnace and predicts baked anode properties.
Provides firing schedule and draft setpoints for target quality at minimum fuel.
p: Multi-section ring furnace firing manually balanced
Baked anode density varies across pits
Fuel cost higher than design
Air leaks and combustion imbalances unknown until lab tests
Difficult to coordinate firing schedule across 32-72 sections
uc.calc: Fuel savings 5-10% on ₹50-100 cr baking fuel + anode quality. ₹5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses thermal imaging of furnace sections, shell temperatures, refractory thickness models and gas leak detection.
Detects refractory thinning, section anomalies, and cross-pit hot/cold spots.
Provides location-tagged maintenance alerts and campaign life prediction.
p: Refractory failure in a section halts furnace operation
Manual inspections miss developing damage
Section repair scheduling reactive
Difficult to plan major furnace overhaul timing
uc.calc: Refractory campaign extension + unplanned shutdown avoidance. ₹1.5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses high-resolution camera feeds and acoustic resonance testing of baked anodes.
Detects cracks, voids, density variations and surface defects before rodding.
Provides quality classification and rejects defective anodes before potline charging.
p: Defective anodes pass to potline causing anode effects (PFC emissions)
Manual visual inspection inconsistent operator-to-operator
Cracks and voids not always visible externally
High AE frequency from undetected anode quality issues
kpi: Anode effect frequency in pots downstream
uc.calc: Anode effect reduction + defective anode rejection. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Alumina (smelter-grade), cryolite, AlF3 (additive)
procs.ut: DC power (massive: 200-500 kA, 4-4.5 V per pot), compressed air
procs.out: Molten aluminium (98-99.7% purity), CO2 + PFCs (anode gases)
procs.q: Current efficiency (CE%), specific energy (kWh/kg Al), pot voltage, bath temperature, AlF3%, alumina concentration%

d: Analyses pot voltage, current, bath temperature, alumina concentration, AlF3 content, anode-cathode distance (ACD), and historical trends per pot.
Models pot electrochemistry and thermal balance; predicts current efficiency (CE) and specific energy versus operating conditions.
Provides advisory on voltage setpoint, beam raise, alumina feed and bath chemistry for maximum CE with stable thermal balance.
p: Pot operations highly variable across potline (no uniform control)
Specific energy higher than design (₹56,000/t Al power cost)
Operator-dependent pot management
Limited visibility into individual pot performance trends
CE degradation often noticed only via lab gravimetry
Pot stability disturbed by alumina feeding or anode change events
uc.calc: Specific energy reduction 0.5-1% on 14 MWh/t Al × ₹4/kWh × 1 MTPA = ₹28-56 cr potential. Realistic capture ₹15 cr/MTPA Al. Plus CE improvement (kg Al per kAh).

d: Critical parameters monitored: anode beam position, individual anode current distribution, pot voltage signature, bath temperature, alumina concentration, bath height, and anode age within cycle.
Analyses these signals (optionally augmented with laser distance or vibration sensors) to build an inferential real-time estimate of anode-cathode distance (ACD) per pot.
Detects ACD drift over the anode cycle (driven by anode consumption + bath height changes + cathode wear) and identifies pots operating at sub-optimal ACD versus target.
Provides beam raise advisory and target ACD per pot, maintaining safety margin against anode-bath shorting while minimizing voltage drop in bath.
p: Direct ACD measurement is difficult (~960°C, hostile environment)
ACD physically measured only during anode change (every 26-28 days)
Voltage proxy for ACD is imperfect (bath chemistry, temperature also affect voltage)
Operators run conservative high ACD to avoid shorting risk (energy penalty)
Each cm of unnecessary ACD costs ~1.5% in specific energy = ₹840/t Al
Pot-to-pot ACD variation not tracked systematically
uc.calc: Each cm ACD reduction = ~1.5% specific energy savings. At 14 MWh/t Al × ₹4/kWh = ₹56,000/t Al power cost. 0.5-1 cm reduction × 1.5%/cm = 0.75-1.5% × ₹56,000/t = ₹420-840/t Al = ₹4.2-8.4 cr/MTPA. Set conservatively at ₹6 cr per MTPA aluminium. Strong complement to Pot Stability & Energy Optimization.

d: Analyses pot voltage trajectory, alumina concentration in bath, anode current distribution and feeder behavior.
Predicts anode effect (AE) onset 3-10 minutes in advance with target pot identification.
Provides corrective action advisory (alumina feed adjustment, beam movement) to prevent AE before it occurs.
p: Anode effects emit PFCs (massive GHG) and waste energy
AE often unpredictable; operator surprise events
CBAM (EU exporters) makes PFCs a financial penalty post-2026
AE recovery disrupts pot stability for hours after the event
No real-time prediction model in current operations
uc.calc: AE frequency reduction 30-50% × 5-10 AE/pot-day × N pots × ₹10,000/event. Plus PFC emission reduction (carbon credit value). ₹8 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses bath samples (NaF/AlF3 ratio, CaF2, MgF2 content), bath temperature, and AlF3 addition rates.
Models bath chemistry equilibrium and predicts impacts on CE, melting point and fluoride emissions.
Provides advisory on AlF3 addition rate and CaF2 management for target bath chemistry.
p: Bath chemistry drifts; manual AlF3 additions
Bath ratio off-target degrades CE silently
Lab analysis lag (4-8 hr) prevents real-time response
AlF3 cost high; over-additions costly and common
Bath chemistry-CE relationship not transparent to operators
uc.calc: Bath chemistry stability improves CE 0.3-0.5% + reduced AlF3 consumption. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

uc.t: Pot Lining Life Prediction & Cathode Health
d: Analyses cathode voltage drop trends, pot-to-pot voltage variation, cathode surface temperature and bath penetration patterns.
Predicts pot lining remaining-useful-life and identifies pots at risk of early failure (tap-out, lining failure).
Provides relining schedule advisory for planned shutdown vs unplanned failure.
p: Pot tap-outs catastrophic and unplanned (₹2-5 cr/event)
Pot lining life varies wildly (1,500-3,000 days)
Relining schedule reactive, not planned
Cathode degradation patterns hidden until late
Difficult to coordinate relining campaigns across potline
uc.calc: Unplanned tap-out prevention (₹2-5 cr/event × 0.5-1/yr) + planned relining cost optimization. ₹5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses tapping crucible weight, metal temperature, tapping duration, post-tap pot conditions and metal quality (Fe, Si pickup).
Detects tap quality issues (poor metal recovery, anode pieces in metal, temperature anomalies).
Provides tap operation advisory and quality flags for downstream casthouse.
p: Tap weight variability affects casthouse planning
Metal Fe/Si pickup during tap affects downstream products
Operator-dependent tap quality
Crucible and transport schedule disruption from tap delays
uc.calc: Metal yield improvement + reduced downstream refining. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses overhead camera feeds of pot bath surface, crust integrity, and anode geometry.
Detects crust breakage, anode shape anomalies, sludge patterns and operator interventions.
Provides quality scoring of pot operations and intervention triggers.
p: Pot disturbances detected late (after temperature/voltage drift)
Crust quality varies; operator visual judgment only
Sludge accumulation patterns not tracked systematically
Intervention timing reactive rather than predictive
uc.calc: Early intervention on pot disturbances + reduced AE. ₹1.5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

uc.t: Cathode Voltage Drop & Current Distribution Optimization
d: Analyses individual cathode collector bar voltages, current distribution across pots, and pot-to-pot voltage variation.
Detects current imbalance, cathode degradation patterns and energy hotspots.
Provides pot-specific advisory for current balancing and potline-wide energy efficiency.
p: Current imbalance hides chronic energy losses
Cathode degradation not visible until tap-out
Pot-line wide imbalance not actively managed
Difficult to attribute energy losses to specific pots
uc.calc: Cathode voltage drop reduction × current × pots. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

loc: Alumina dense-phase conveying lines (silos to day bins, day bins to point feeders)
Crucible handling for hot metal tapping (heavy load + molten metal safety)
Anode handling cranes (heavy baked anodes to pots, anode butts return)
d: Analyses camera feeds, vibration on handling equipment and motor signals.
Detects belt/crane damage, alumina conveying anomalies and material handling jams.
Provides location-tagged alerts before downtime.
p: Alumina dense-phase conveying lines can plug or wear
Crucible handling involves molten metal (safety + downtime)
Anode handling crane downtime stops anode changes
Material handling failures impact pot operation indirectly
uc.calc: Alumina conveying reliability + anode handling. ₹0.5 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Pot gas (CO2, PFCs, HF, SO2, fluoride dust)
procs.out: Captured pot gas to GTC, fugitive emissions (managed)
procs.q: Hood capture efficiency%, fugitive emissions, fluoride emission rate

d: Analyses thermal and visual camera feeds of pot hoods, fluoride sensors near pots, and ID fan duty.
Detects hood damage, poor sealing, fugitive emissions and unhooded pot operations.
Provides immediate alerts for hood repair and operational corrections.
p: Damaged hoods leak fluoride (worker exposure + compliance risk)
Hood gasket failures not visible until inspection
Pots opened for crane access have temporary high emissions
Manual hood inspection coverage limited
GTC fluoride load varies due to inconsistent hood capture
uc.calc: Hood capture improvement 2-5% × fluoride recovery value + compliance. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Calcined alumina (from calcination), fluoride additives
procs.out: Controlled alumina delivery to each pot (point feeders or central feeders)
procs.q: Feeding rate accuracy, dust generation, alumina concentration in bath

d: Analyses point feeder cycle times, alumina delivery rates, dense-phase conveying pressure and bath alumina concentration.
Detects feeder under/over delivery, plugging events, and pots with chronic feeding issues.
Provides feeder calibration advisory and pot-specific feeding adjustments.
p: Point feeders drift between calibrations
Plug events cause local bath alumina deficiency → anode effect risk
Manual feeder checks miss developing issues
Pot-to-pot feeding inconsistency
uc.calc: Feeder reliability reduces AE frequency + pot disturbance events. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Molten Al from pots, alloying additions (Si, Mg, Cu, Zn, Fe, Mn, Ti master alloys), recycled scrap
procs.ut: NG/HFO/induction power, refining chemicals (flux, Cl2 for degassing)
procs.out: Treated molten Al at target composition and quality
procs.q: Composition (per alloy spec), hydrogen content (Reduced Pressure Test), inclusion level, temperature

d: Analyses fuel firing rate, air ratio, furnace temperature profile, metal temperature and melt loss rates.
Models combustion versus melt quality and predicts fuel consumption per t metal treated.
Provides fuel/air setpoint advisory for target temperature with minimum fuel and minimum melt loss.
p: Fuel consumption higher than design (no AI optimization)
Melt loss (oxide skim) varies and is direct revenue loss
Manual burner adjustments based on operator experience
Furnace efficiency degrades over campaign
uc.calc: Fuel savings 3-5% + melt loss reduction 0.1-0.2%. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses incoming metal composition, alloying material additions, mixing time and spectrometer feedback.
Builds soft sensor for in-process composition between spectrometer samples.
Provides real-time composition predictions and addition advisory to hit alloy spec with minimum corrective additions.
p: Spectrometer sampling lag (10-20 min) drives over-additions
Master alloy overshoot common (operator caution)
Rework cycles delay casting schedule
Composition variance affects downstream rolling quality
uc.calc: Alloying material savings + reduced rework. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses degasser rotor speed, Ar/Cl2 flow, melt hydrogen content (RPT, Alspek), and inclusion monitoring data.
Models degassing kinetics and predicts hydrogen and inclusion levels in cast metal.
Provides degasser setpoint advisory for target metal quality with minimum gas consumption.
p: Degasser performance varies; operator-driven
Hydrogen and inclusion sampling slow (lab tests)
Gas overconsumption (cautious operation)
Downstream defects traced to inadequate degassing
uc.calc: Gas consumption reduction + downstream defect reduction. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Treated molten Al, casting molds, lubricants
procs.out: Cast products (sheet ingots, extrusion billets, T-bars, foundry ingots)
procs.q: Surface quality (cracks, segregation), internal defects, geometric tolerance, hot cracking

uc.t: DC Casting Surface Quality & Defect Detection
d: Analyses high-resolution camera feeds of cast surface, infrared thermal feeds and casting process parameters (water flow, mold motion).
Detects surface cracks, cold shuts, segregation patterns and hot cracking in real time.
Provides immediate alerts to operators with corrective action advisory.
p: Casting defects discovered post-cast (sometimes after machining)
Manual visual inspection inconsistent
Hot crack and cold shut defects expensive
Casting parameter drift hard to catch in real time
uc.calc: Reject reduction × cast product value. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Analyses camera feeds and laser scanner data of cast billets/slabs for dimensions and surface finish.
Detects out-of-spec dimensions, surface marks and machining requirements.
Provides quality scoring and routing decisions for downstream processing.
p: Manual dimensional inspection slow
Out-of-spec product reaches downstream
Difficult to track gradual drift in dimensions
Manual measurement variability between inspectors
uc.calc: Automated inspection + downstream rework reduction. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: As-cast aluminium billets/slabs
procs.out: Homogenized billets/slabs ready for downstream processing
procs.q: Homogenization temperature uniformity, soak time, surface oxidation, mechanical properties

d: Analyses furnace zone temperatures, soaking time, billet load and product property targets.
Models homogenization kinetics and predicts mechanical property achievement.
Provides cycle optimization for target properties at minimum energy and cycle time.
p: Homogenization cycle conservative (long for safety margin)
Energy consumption high
Mechanical property variability
Schedule constraints from cycle uncertainty
uc.calc: Energy savings + cycle time reduction. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Cast sheet ingots (homogenized, ~600mm thick)
procs.out: Preheated ingots (~500-550°C) ready for hot rolling
procs.q: Temperature uniformity, scale formation %, soak time, surface oxidation

d: Analyses fuel firing rate, zone temperatures, sheet ingot surface temperature profile and scale formation data.
Models heating kinetics and predicts ingot core temperature uniformity and scale loss versus operating conditions.
Provides advisory on zone temperature setpoints and soak time for target uniformity at minimum fuel.
p: Fuel cost rising; consumption above design specification
Scale loss is direct revenue loss (~1% yield)
Manual zone temperature control by operators
Cycle conservative for safety; longer than necessary
Energy consumption above benchmark
uc.calc: Fuel savings 3-5% × ₹50-80 cr/MTPA preheat fuel + scale loss reduction 0.3-0.5%. ₹2 cr per MTPA rolled product.

procs.rm: Preheated sheet ingots
procs.ut: Electric power (mill drives), cooling water (roll bite), lubricant
procs.out: Hot band coils (~3-6mm thick)
procs.q: Gauge, surface quality, profile, edge condition, microstructure

d: Analyses mill load distribution, rolling schedule, entry/exit temperatures, sheet ingot variability and downstream quality feedback.
Models rolling kinetics and predicts surface quality, gauge variance and throughput versus operating conditions.
Provides rolling schedule, pass reduction and speed advisory for target quality with maximum throughput.
p: HRM throughput is often binding plant constraint
Quality variability causes downstream rework
Operator-dependent rolling schedules
Roll changes interrupt production
Manual process tuning per coil
uc.calc: Throughput uplift 2-3% × rolling margin ₹40,000/t × 1 MTPA = ₹8-12 cr potential; capture 30-50% = ₹4 cr per MTPA rolled.

d: Analyses high-speed line scan camera feeds across the full strip width at multiple points along the mill.
Detects rolling marks, surface scratches, edge cracks, slivers and dirt embedded defects.
Provides defect classification with CD/MD location and triggers operator alerts for root cause investigation.
p: Defects cause customer rejects (₹15,000-40,000/t)
Manual sampling insufficient
Defect root cause investigation slow
Mill condition issues hidden
Quality scoring inconsistent across operators
uc.calc: Reject reduction 0.5-1% × rolled product margin ₹40-60K/t. ₹3 cr per MTPA rolled.

d: Analyses roll force trends, mill motor signatures, roll temperature profiles and surface quality correlation with roll life.
Predicts roll wear patterns and end-of-life for each work roll and back-up roll.
Provides roll change scheduling and roll life optimization advisory.
p: Roll wear impacts surface quality
Manual roll inspection only during changes
Roll change scheduling reactive
Premature changes waste roll life
Grinding cost high
uc.calc: Roll life extension 10-15% + reduced surface defects from roll degradation. ₹2 cr per MTPA rolled.

procs.rm: Hot band coils, rolling lubricant
procs.ut: Electric power (mill drives), cooling water, lubricant management
procs.out: Cold rolled coils (0.2-3mm gauge typical)
procs.q: Thickness variance (μm), profile, flatness (I-units), surface, yield%

d: Analyses online X-ray gauge data, profile/flatness measurements, mill load profile, entry coil variability and lubricant condition.
Models cold rolling response and predicts thickness, profile and flatness deviations.
Provides rolling schedule, pass reduction and tension advisory for tighter quality.
p: Off-spec thickness causes customer rejection
Profile/flatness defects expensive in cold rolled grades
Manual rolling parameter tuning per coil
Hot band entry variability hard to compensate
Quality root cause investigation slow
uc.calc: Gauge reduction 1-2% achievable × cold rolled product margin ₹50,000-70,000/t. ₹5 cr per MTPA cold rolled.

d: Analyses high-resolution line scan camera feeds across the cold rolled strip.
Detects surface scratches, rolling marks, lube spots, edge cracks and inclusion defects.
Provides defect classification, location tracking and root cause analysis tools.
p: Surface defects in CRM are expensive (₹50,000-70,000/t product)
Manual sampling slow
Defect investigation manual
Operator-dependent quality scoring
Customer audits frequent for cold rolled grades
uc.calc: Reject reduction 0.5-1% × cold rolled margin ₹60K/t = ₹3-6 cr/MTPA. ₹4 cr per MTPA cold rolled.

d: Analyses roll force trends, mill motor signatures, surface quality correlation and lubricant degradation.
Predicts roll wear and surface degradation; recommends grinding cycles and roll changes.
Provides roll life optimization advisory.
p: Cold mill roll quality is critical for surface finish
Manual roll inspection
Roll changes interrupt production
Premature changes waste roll life
Quality issues from roll wear hidden
uc.calc: Roll life extension + surface quality. ₹2 cr per MTPA cold rolled.

procs.rm: Cold rolled coils (intermediate or final)
procs.ut: NG/electric, protective atmosphere (N2 for some grades)
procs.out: Annealed coils with target mechanical properties
procs.q: Mechanical properties (UTS, YS, elongation), gauge tolerance, surface, microstructure

d: Analyses furnace zone temperatures, soak time, coil load and mechanical property results from lab testing.
Models annealing kinetics and predicts mechanical property achievement.
Provides cycle optimization for target properties at minimum energy and cycle time.
p: Annealing cycles conservative (long for safety margin)
Energy consumption high vs benchmark
Property variability between batches
Manual cycle setting per alloy
Cycle uncertainty creates schedule constraints
uc.calc: Energy reduction 5-10% + cycle time reduction 10-15%. ₹3 cr per MTPA annealed.

procs.rm: Light gauge cold rolled coil, rolling oil
procs.ut: Electric power (high specific consumption), rolling oil management
procs.out: Aluminium foil (down to 6μm for capacitor/packaging)
procs.q: Pinhole density (#/m²), gauge variance, surface quality, mechanical properties

d: Analyses high-resolution line scan camera and laser/optical pinhole detection systems across foil strip.
Detects pinholes, gauge variations, surface streaks, oil stains and edge defects.
Provides defect classification with pinhole density mapping; triggers operator alerts and coil quality grading.
p: Pinholes cause major customer rejection (food/pharma foil grades)
Manual sampling insufficient for foil products
Gauge variance affects yield
Foil products are premium (₹4-6 lakh/t)
Customer specs tight (especially for capacitor and pharma foil)
uc.calc: Reject reduction 1-2% × foil margin ₹2-3 lakh/t = ₹2-6 cr/MTPA. ₹4 cr per MTPA foil.

procs.rm: Extrusion billets (6063, 6061, 7075 grades typical)
procs.out: Preheated billets (~450-500°C) at target uniformity for extrusion
procs.q: Billet temperature uniformity, scale loss%, surface oxidation, soak time

d: Analyses billet entry temperature, zone temperatures (typically induction or gas-fired), soak time and billet exit temperature uniformity.
Models heating profile and predicts billet exit conditions for extrusion press readiness.
Provides zone setpoint advisory for target uniformity at minimum fuel.
p: Manual zone control by operators
Fuel cost rising
Cycle conservative for safety
Temperature uniformity affects extrusion quality
Scale loss is direct yield loss
uc.calc: Fuel savings 3-5% × billet preheat energy + yield improvement. ₹2 cr per MTPA extruded.

procs.rm: Preheated extrusion billets, dies, lubricants
procs.ut: Hydraulic power, water (press quench), die heating
procs.out: Extruded shapes (profiles for automotive, architectural, structural)
procs.q: Surface finish, dimensional tolerance, mechanical properties, mechanical defects

d: Analyses ram speed, press force, billet temperature, die exit temperature, profile dimensions and downstream quality.
Models extrusion kinetics and predicts press output, surface quality and yield versus operating conditions.
Provides advisory on ram speed, billet preheat target and die management for maximum output at target quality.
p: Press speed conservatively set (safety + quality margin)
Yield variability across alloys and profiles
Die wear hidden until profile defects emerge
Manual ram speed control per profile
Quality vs throughput tradeoff manual
uc.calc: Throughput uplift 3-5% × extrusion margin ₹40-60K/t × 1 MTPA = ₹12-30 cr potential; capture 30% = ₹5 cr per MTPA extruded.

d: Analyses high-resolution camera and laser profile scanner feeds at the press exit and stretcher.
Detects surface defects (die marks, scratches, blister), dimensional anomalies and stretching issues.
Provides defect classification with profile-specific routing decisions.
p: Extrusion defects cause customer rejection (architectural grade especially)
Manual inspection slow
Die marks hidden until customer audit
Dimensional tolerance compliance variable
Surface defects discovered downstream
uc.calc: Reject reduction × extrusion margin. ₹3 cr per MTPA extruded.

procs.rm: Extruded profiles (post-press, post-stretching)
procs.out: Aged extrusions with final mechanical properties (T5/T6 tempers)
procs.q: Mechanical properties (UTS, YS, hardness), temper compliance, surface

d: Analyses aging furnace zone temperatures, soak time, load profile and resulting mechanical property data.
Models aging kinetics for different temper specifications (T5, T6).
Provides cycle optimization for target properties at minimum energy and time.
p: Aging cycles conservative (long for safety)
Energy consumption high
Property variability between batches
Manual cycle setting per alloy/temper
Schedule constraints from cycle uncertainty
uc.calc: Energy reduction + cycle time. ₹2 cr per MTPA aged.

procs.rm: Finished coils (cold rolled, foil, or coated)
procs.out: Customer-spec rolls (slit width) or cut sheets
procs.q: Edge condition, slit accuracy, trim quality, dimensional tolerance

d: Analyses camera feeds of slit edges and side trim removal at the slitting line.
Detects edge cracks, ragged edges, knife wear effects and trim handling issues.
Provides knife change recommendations and quality alerts.
p: Edge cracks from slit knives cause customer rejects
Knife change scheduling reactive
Trim handling jams
Edge quality varies operator to operator
Manual inspection inconsistent
uc.calc: Edge defect reduction + knife optimization. ₹2 cr per MTPA finished.

procs.rm: Finished customer rolls, wrapping materials, end caps, labels
procs.ut: Power (line drives), compressed air, packaging materials
procs.out: Wrapped and packaged rolls/extrusions ready for dispatch
procs.q: Wrap integrity, label accuracy, end cap quality, dispatch readiness

d: Analyses camera feeds at the wrapping line, label scanners and packaging seal integrity sensors.
Detects wrapping defects, missing labels, damaged outer wrap and end cap issues.
Provides dispatch quality scoring and alerts before shipment.
p: Packaging defects cause customer returns
Label mismatches lead to dispute
Manual quality checks slow
Wrap integrity variable
End cap defects cause transit damage
uc.calc: Customer claim reduction + dispatch quality. ₹1 cr per MTPA finished.

procs.rm: Coal (mostly), some biomass, makeup water
procs.ut: Combustion air, makeup water, chemicals (DM water treatment)
procs.out: DC power (after rectification) to potline, HP steam, ash
procs.q: Heat rate (kCal/kWh), generation cost (₹/kWh), availability%, emissions (NOx, SOx, PM)

uc.t: CPP Heat Rate & Generation Cost Optimization
d: Analyses boiler combustion (coal quality, air/fuel ratio, flue gas), turbine performance (heat rate, vacuum), and rectifier efficiency.
Models plant-wide heat rate versus load and conditions; predicts generation cost (₹/kWh).
Provides operating advisory for optimal load distribution and emissions compliance.
p: Heat rate drifts up over time (boiler/turbine fouling)
Generation cost not fully attributed to operating decisions
Coal quality variability impacts efficiency
Multiple units; load distribution suboptimal
Emission compliance margin shrinking
uc.calc: Heat rate improvement 1-2% × ₹100-150 cr/MTPA Al CPP fuel cost. ₹6 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Pot gases (CO2, HF, SO2, fluoride dust, PFCs)
procs.ut: Fresh alumina (for fluoride adsorption), power, compressed air
procs.out: Cleaned gas to stack (within emission limits), fluoride-loaded alumina back to potline
procs.q: HF emission (mg/Nm3), particulate emission, fluoride recovery%, alumina recirculation rate

uc.t: GTC Fluoride Capture & Alumina Reuse Optimization
d: Analyses HF emissions, particulate emissions, alumina circulation rate, reactor pressure drop and bag filter performance.
Models fluoride adsorption kinetics and predicts capture efficiency.
Provides alumina circulation and reactor setpoint advisory for target emissions with minimum fresh alumina.
p: Fluoride emission compliance limit getting tighter
GTC alumina circulation manually set
Pot gas variability not tracked into GTC operation
Reactor performance drops between maintenance
Bag filter performance not monitored proactively
uc.calc: Fluoride recovery + compliance margin + AlF3 makeup reduction. ₹4 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: HP/MP/LP steam from CPP + Bayer process
procs.out: Steam delivered to Bayer digesters, calcination drying, holding furnaces, aux services
procs.q: Header pressures, flow distribution, condensate recovery%, venting losses

d: Analyses steam flows, pressures and consumption across plant (CPP, Bayer digesters, calciner, holding furnaces).
Models steam balance and identifies inefficient consumers, venting losses and trap failures.
Provides plant-wide optimization advisory for steam distribution.
p: Steam traps fail silently
Condensate flooding common in some sections
Vent losses during transients
PRDS sluggish in following load changes
uc.calc: Network optimization 2-3% on total steam value. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

loc: Bayer digestion HP steam headers and drip legs (highest steam pressure, largest losses if failed)
Heat exchanger and process equipment drains across the refinery
Holding furnace and casthouse auxiliary steam consumers
Distribution and tracing line drainage points across the plant
d: Analyses inlet and outlet temperature signatures from wireless battery-powered sensors deployed at each steam trap.
Detects failed-open (steam passing through), failed-closed (condensate backup), and failed-cold (dead) conditions using temperature delta logic.
Provides location-tagged alerts to maintenance for proactive replacement, replacing annual audit cycles with continuous monitoring.
p: 10-25% of steam traps fail at any given time (industry baseline)
Annual ultrasonic audits cost time and labor, and miss interim failures
Failed-open traps waste ₹2-25 lakh per trap per year in steam
Failed-closed traps cause water hammer and equipment damage
No continuous monitoring at scale (plant has 1,000-3,000 traps)
Manual inspection rotation cannot cover the full trap population
kpi: Steam loss from failed traps (t/yr or ₹/yr)
uc.calc: Trap failure rate 15% × 1,000 traps × ₹2 lakh/yr avg loss × 50% capture = ₹1.5 cr/MTPA aluminium. Plus equipment protection from water hammer events.

procs.rm: Refinery effluent, red mud (high alkalinity), industrial wastewater
procs.out: Treated effluent (within state PCB limits), red mud to safe disposal
procs.q: Outlet pH, BOD, COD, TSS, heavy metals; red mud storage compliance

d: Analyses inlet effluent (pH, alkalinity, TSS, heavy metals), treatment chemicals, red mud thickener performance and disposal yard conditions.
Models treatment kinetics and predicts compliance margins.
Provides chemical dosing and disposal operations advisory.
p: Effluent quality varies; chemicals overdosed for safety
Red mud disposal logistics constrained
Regulatory inspection visits frequent
Treatment failures expensive (penalty + reputation)
Manual chemical dosing common
uc.calc: Chemical optimization + compliance margin + disposal cost. ₹2 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Atmospheric air, raw water, makeup water
procs.out: Compressed air for actuators, instruments, alumina conveying; cooling water for casthouse, GTC
procs.q: Air dewpoint, pressure (bar), flow (Nm3/h), cooling water temp ΔT, conductivity

uc.t: Compressed Air & Cooling Water Network Optimization
d: Analyses compressor load, network pressure, cooling water ΔT, pump efficiencies and consumer demand patterns.
Detects compressor cycling, leaks, cooling tower fouling and pump degradation.
Provides operating advisory for both networks.
p: Compressed air leaks accumulate; never fully addressed
Cooling tower fouling reduces capacity over time
Pump efficiency drops gradually
Network demand variability not visible
uc.calc: Leak reduction + pump efficiency + cooling tower performance. ₹1 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: OT data (DCS/PLC tags), MES, ERP, lab data (LIMS), pot controllers (PMS), IoT streams
procs.ut: Edge gateways, network infrastructure, cloud compute, storage
procs.out: Unified data layer enabling all AI use cases; pot, refinery, casthouse contextual model
procs.q: Tag coverage%, data quality, latency, uptime, governance compliance

uc.vt: Enabler for all other use cases (no standalone ₹ impact)
d: Foundational data layer: unified namespace, historian access, pot management system (PMS) integration, MES, ERP linkage.
Enables every other AI use case by providing reliable, tagged, contextual data across the plant.
Provides time-series storage, governance, role-based access and edge-to-cloud connectivity.
p: Plant data scattered across DCS, PLC, lab, ERP systems
No single source of truth across the plant
Analytics projects start with data plumbing every time
Tag naming inconsistent across systems
Limited self-service for plant teams
uc.calc: Enabler — value realized through downstream use cases.

procs.rm: Lab samples, online quality sensors (XRF, ICP-OES), customer specs, ASI standards
procs.ut: Lab instruments, LIMS infrastructure, calibration standards
procs.out: Quality intelligence dashboards, COA, traceability records, SPC charts
procs.q: Spec compliance%, lab turnaround time, COA accuracy, certified product%

Provides early warning on quality drift and faster lab-to-process feedback loops.

Quality data in silos (Bayer, smelter, casthouse)
Quality trends not visible cross-functionally
Root cause analysis manual and slow
Customer audit prep labor-intensive
uc.calc: Quality drift reduction + off-spec production reduction. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: Sensor data (vibration, temp, oil, motor current), maintenance history, spare parts data
procs.ut: Edge processing, CBM platform, CMMS software, MRO inventory system
procs.out: Failure predictions, work orders, reliability KPIs (MTBF, MTTR), optimized spares
procs.q: Equipment availability%, MTBF, MTTR, maintenance cost/t Al, unplanned downtime hours

Provides location-tagged alerts and RUL estimates for planned interventions.

High maintenance + production loss cost
Aging asset base needs proactive management
uc.calc: Unplanned downtime reduction × Al margin × hours saved. ₹15 cr per MTPA aluminium.

d: Workflow management for maintenance work orders, planned/unplanned work tracking, asset history and maintenance KPIs.

Provides asset-level reliability metrics (MTBF, MTTR), maintenance cost reporting and compliance audit trails.

No structured asset history
Spare consumption not attributed accurately
Audit prep labor-intensive

d: Analyses spare parts inventory, lead times, criticality, consumption patterns and supplier reliability for refinery + smelter + CPP spares.
Models optimal stocking levels, reorder points and consignment opportunities for critical spares.
Provides inventory optimization advisory and supplier performance dashboards.

Critical spares stockouts cause emergencies
Lead times not tracked systematically
Cataloging inconsistent
Supplier performance not tracked
uc.calc: Inventory reduction 15-25% × cost of capital + emergency procurement savings. ₹3 cr per MTPA aluminium.

procs.rm: CCTV feeds, gas detection (HF, SO2), access control, incident history

Incident investigation slow
